summary: stui attaches a terminal on its own host to the local PTY session and one on another fleet host over Fabric, never through a daemon; fleet members no longer fall back to the client gateway for terminals

replay.detail: No replay, backfill, stored data or transcript change.

schema.detail: Published schema, operations and contract digest are unchanged. The client reads the daemon's existing local-terminal and fleet-membership routes and accepts the core API error shape on them.

rules.detail: No claim, checkpoint, retention or authority rule change. The person's terminal.read and terminal.control grants are checked before any Fabric dial, as st terminals attach checks them.

compatibility.detail: stui on a machine with its own daemon no longer falls back to the client gateway for a terminal on another host: the owner must run st terminals expose-fabric and grant this machine st3/pty/FLEET_ID, or stui says Fabric did not reach it. Paired devices without a daemon keep the gateway. A newer stui against an older daemon on the same machine, one without the local-terminal route, treats a local terminal as remote and shows a Fabric error until that daemon restarts onto the new build, so restart the daemon before or with stui. Swift and TypeScript clients and the wire are unchanged.

downtime.detail: Ordinary rolling deployment; no data conversion or extra startup work.

manual.detail: Before this stui attaches a remote terminal, each fleet host runs st terminals expose-fabric and allows st3/pty/FLEET_ID for the other fleet hosts' Fabric peers, then fabric reload-peers. Restart the local daemon onto the same build as stui.

recovery.detail: No recovery, durable payload or initialization changes.
